sheet-54.description: The northern part of Hasbrouck Heights, printed as sheet 62 ('New Sheet, Oct. 1923') at 100 ft to an inch. Grandview Boulevard crosses the top of the sheet, with a trolley right of way running beside it and curving away to the north at the top right. Below it Ottawa, Paterson, Bell, Lawrence, Williams, Stanley and Longworth Avenues run down the sheet, crossed by Collins Avenue, Burton Avenue, Terrace Avenue, Crescent Avenue and Prospect Avenue; at the lower left Hillside Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Hasbrouck Avenue form a smaller grid between Ottawa and Lawrence. The area is a residential subdivision with many vacant lots and scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, several rows marked 'from plans'. Named buildings include the Lincoln Public School at Burton and Ottawa Avenues and the Hasbrouck Heights Garage at Terrace and Ottawa Avenues; a fire alarm bell on a steel tower stands between Williams and Stanley Avenues. Fire alarm boxes are marked at Grandview Boulevard and Lawrence Avenue and at Terrace Avenue. Water pipes of 6 to 24 inches are drawn along Burton and Terrace Avenues and several cross streets. The lower part of the sheet, south of Hasbrouck and Prospect Avenues, is large blocks with almost no buildings, and the southeast corner is left blank.
notes: The manifest labels this canvas 'Sheet 54'; the printed sheet number is 62.
Grandview Boulevard is 'Boulevard' in OpenStreetMap; Prospect Avenue is Prospect Street.
Crescent Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Trolley right of way beside Grandview Boulevard.

Printed sheet 62 (canvas labelled 54), 'New Sheet Oct. 1923', Hasbrouck Heights, 100 ft. One part. Streets: Grandview Blvd, Burton, Terrace, Prospect, Hasbrouck, Collins, Crescent Avs; Ottawa, Paterson, Bell, Lawrence, Williams, Stanley, Longworth, Hillside Avs. Trolley right of way along Grandview at top right.

sheet-62.description: The boundary of Carlstadt and Wood-Ridge, printed as sheet 65 ('Add'l Sheet, Oct. 1923') at 100 ft to an inch. The Carlstadt and Wood-Ridge borough line runs down the upper left and then along Franklin Street and Passaic Avenue, so the large open tract at the top left (block 9 and the upper part of block 8, with a few scattered buildings) lies in Carlstadt and the rest in Wood-Ridge. Garden, Washington and Franklin Streets cross the upper half; below them a grid of Madison, James and Rose Streets and Charter Oak is laid out between Passaic Avenue at the left edge and Central Avenue, with Union Avenue running down the middle of the sheet. East of Union Avenue the numbered streets, 11th Street to 2nd Street, cross Main Avenue and North Avenue; between 7th and 5th Streets a crescent-shaped park block is drawn. The area is residential: small frame dwellings on narrow lots, many vacant, a few brick or tile dwellings and stores, and a small group of tile buildings marked 'from plans' near Union Avenue at 8th Street. A small novelty works stands on Passaic Avenue near James Street. Water pipes of 6 to 24 inches are drawn along 5th, 4th and 3rd Streets, Union Avenue and Main Avenue.
notes: The manifest labels this canvas 'Sheet 62'; the printed sheet number is 65.
Renamed since: Central Avenue is Center Street, Passaic Avenue is Fritsch Avenue, Madison (west of Union Avenue) is 5th Street, James is 4th Street and Charter Oak is Charter Oak Street.
Wood-Ridge is spelled Woodridge on the sheet.

Printed sheet 65 (canvas labelled 62), 'Add'l Sheet Oct. 1923', Carlstadt and Wood-Ridge, 100 ft. One part. West half Carlstadt/Wood-Ridge (Garden, Washington, Franklin, Madison, James, Rose, Charter Oak; Passaic Av, Central Av), east half Wood-Ridge (Union Av, Main Av, North Av, 2nd to 11th Sts). Large blank block 8 at top.

sheet-65.description: The northern part of Wood-Ridge, printed as sheet 66 ('Add'l Sheet, Oct. 1923') at 100 ft to an inch. North Avenue runs along the left edge, with Woodridge Avenue, Columbia Boulevard and Highland Avenue parallel to it; 11th, 10th and 7th Streets cross them in the upper half, Valley Boulevard cuts diagonally across the lower half, and Hillcrest Avenue runs along the bottom. The ends of 9th, 8th, 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd Streets and Franklin Street are named in the left margin where they meet North Avenue on the adjoining sheet 65. The drawn area is a residential subdivision of narrow lots with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, more densely built along Woodridge Avenue and Columbia Boulevard, where a row of tile dwellings stands, and a bakery near Woodridge Avenue and Valley Boulevard. The eastern half of the sheet, east of Highland Avenue, is two large undivided blocks (102 and 103) with no buildings; Valley Boulevard is drawn through them, and a dash-dot match line marked A and B runs down the right side. Water pipes of 6 to 24 inches run along 7th Street, Woodridge Avenue, Columbia Boulevard, Valley Boulevard and Hillcrest Avenue.
notes: The manifest labels this canvas 'Sheet 65'; the printed sheet number is 66.
Wood-Ridge is spelled Woodridge on the sheet.

Printed sheet 66 (canvas labelled 65), 'Add'l Sheet Oct. 1923', Wood-Ridge, 100 ft. One part. North Av, Woodridge Av, Columbia Blvd, Highland Av; 7th, 10th, 11th Sts, Valley Blvd, Hillcrest Av. East half blank (blocks 102, 103).

sheet-66.description: Part of Lodi east of Union Street, printed as sheet 67 ('Add'l Sheet, Oct. 1923') at 100 ft to an inch. Union Street runs down the left edge; St. Joseph, with the Public Service Railway Company trolley right of way, runs down the middle, then Church, a street marked 'Not named', and a long blank strip at the right. Between St. Joseph and Church a series of short 30 ft streets cross: Ragonese, Prince, Roosevelt Place, James Place, Division, Carmine and Ford; the wider cross streets Chrystie, Stokes, Christopher and Savoie continue east of Church. West of St. Joseph, James Place and Leo Place run from Union Street, and the rest of that side is deep lots facing Union Street (blocks 97 and 125) with dwellings and a bowling alley. The blocks between St. Joseph and Church are cut into very narrow lots, built up with brick and frame dwellings near the top; east of Church the lots are mostly vacant and the eastern third of the sheet (blocks 302 to 311) is undivided land with no buildings. Water pipes of 4 to 6 inches are drawn along Leo Place, Christopher, Church and St. Joseph.
notes: The manifest labels this canvas 'Sheet 66'; the printed sheet number is 67.
St. Joseph is Saint Joseph Boulevard and Chrystie is Christie Street in OpenStreetMap; Christopher continues west of Saint Joseph as Leo Place.
Prince and Carmine are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Public Service Railway Company trolley right of way along St. Joseph.

Printed sheet 67 (canvas labelled 66), 'Add'l Sheet Oct. 1923', Lodi, 100 ft. One part. Union Av at left, St. Joseph (trolley right of way), Church, a 'Not named' street; cross streets Chrystie, Ragonese, Prince, Stokes, Roosevelt Pl, James Pl, Leo Pl, Christopher, Division, Carmine, Savoie, Ford. East third blank.

sheet-67.description: A long strip of Lodi along Garibaldi Avenue, printed as sheet 68 ('Add'l Sheet, Oct. 1923') at 100 ft to an inch. Garibaldi Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet from a dash-dot match line (A to B) at the top to the Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights borough line, which crosses the bottom of the sheet diagonally. On each side a single row of narrow lots is drawn, and four short streets marked 'Not named' cross or meet the avenue: one leading east near the top, one leading west just below it, and two crossing streets in the lower third. West of the lots runs the old railroad right of way (abandoned), and beyond it a large undivided tract (block 122); east of the lots is another large tract (block 224) with only a few small buildings. The lots along Garibaldi Avenue carry scattered small frame dwellings, a few concrete-block buildings and stores and a tailor shop. A 6-inch water pipe runs down Garibaldi Avenue. The left and right halves of the sheet are otherwise blank.
notes: The manifest labels this canvas 'Sheet 67'; the printed sheet number is 68.
The four 'Not named' streets are, from top to bottom, Meta Lane, Short Street, Pauline Terrace and Wisse Street in OpenStreetMap (identified by their spacing along Garibaldi Avenue).
Old railroad right of way (abandoned) west of the Garibaldi Avenue lots.

Printed sheet 68 (canvas labelled 67), 'Add'l Sheet Oct. 1923', Lodi, 100 ft. One part. Garibaldi Av with three 'Not named' cross streets, old railroad right of way (abandoned) to the west, Lodi / Hasbrouck Heights borough line at bottom. Mostly blank.

sheet-68.description: The boundary area of Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights, printed as sheet 54 ('New Sheet, Oct. 1923') at 100 ft to an inch and turned on the page, with north towards the upper left. Woodside Avenue runs down the left edge, Oak Grove Avenue down the middle and Grandview Boulevard down the right edge; Union Street and Williams Avenue, Lawrence, Bell, Paterson, Ottowa, Lasalle, Madison and Central Avenues and Washington Park and Washington Avenue cross them. The Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights borough line runs along Oak Grove Avenue in the upper half and then turns across the blocks between Paterson and Ottowa Avenues, so the upper left blocks are in Lodi and the rest in Hasbrouck Heights. Almost every block is subdivided into narrow lots, most of them vacant; dwellings are concentrated along Lawrence Avenue, near Grandview Boulevard and along Central and Washington Avenues east of Oak Grove, with a few brick or tile houses. Fire alarm boxes stand on Grandview Boulevard at Lawrence and Central Avenues. Water pipes of 6 inches run along Lawrence, Madison and Central Avenues. The margins name Hunter Street and Monroe Street, which continue on the adjoining Lodi sheet 69.
notes: The manifest labels this canvas 'Sheet 68'; the printed sheet number is 54.
Sheet turned on the page: north points to the upper left.
Ottowa Avenue is Ottawa Avenue, Grandview Boulevard is 'Boulevard', and Washington Park and Washington Avenue are Washington Place in OpenStreetMap.
Union Street (Lodi) and Williams Avenue (Hasbrouck Heights) are the same row of the sheet, meeting at Oak Grove Avenue.

Printed sheet 54 (canvas labelled 68), 'New Sheet Oct. 1923', Lodi and Hasbrouck Heights, 100 ft. One part, turned on the page (north arrow points up-left). Woodside, Oak Grove Avs and Grandview Blvd across; Union/Williams, Lawrence, Bell, Paterson, Ottowa, Lasalle, Madison, Central, Washington Avs.

sheet-69.description: The southern part of the Borough of Lodi between the Saddle River and the Hasbrouck Heights borough line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch on an additional sheet dated October 1923. The Saddle River winds across the top edge, with South Main Street running below it on a slant; a short street marked 'Not opened' leads down to the river. Below Main Street a regular grid is laid out: Norwood, Terrace, McKinley, Kipp and Central Avenues run down the sheet, with Adams Place and Lincoln Place between Main Street and Prospect, and Hunter at the right edge; Lafayette Place, Prospect, Roosevelt Avenue, Hillcrest Avenue, Grove, Madison Place, Jefferson Avenue and Jackson Place cross them, and Woodside Avenue, along the borough line, closes the bottom. Sheridan and Monroe run south from Grove to Woodside. The district is almost wholly residential: narrow lots, most still vacant, with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings and a few stores and brick or tile dwellings. The Lincoln Public School stands at the top right corner. At the lower left a small court, Lafayette Court, is marked 'arbitrary', and a large irregular tract south of Grove between Terrace and Kipp Avenues is crossed by diagonal property lines and left mostly undeveloped. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are drawn along several streets. The bottom margin carries the borough line, lettered Borough of Lodi above and Borough of Hasbrouck Heights below.
notes: Grove is Grove Street, Prospect is Prospect Street, Sheridan is Sheridan Street, Monroe is Monroe Street and Hunter is Hunter Street in OpenStreetMap.
Madison Place is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Lincoln Public School at the corner of South Main Street and Hunter.

Printed sheet 69, 'Add'l Sheet Oct. 1923', Lodi, 100 ft. One part. Saddle River and S. Main St at top; Norwood, Terrace, McKinley, Kipp, Central, Hunter Avs; Lafayette Pl, Prospect, Roosevelt, Hillcrest, Grove, Madison Pl, Jefferson, Jackson Pl, Woodside Av; Adams, Lincoln Pls, Sheridan, Monroe.
